summary: Iteration 14 review — multi-vendor devices + SNMP + topology + retention + blocked-port hint. Backend pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration14.py = 24/24 PASS. Frontend Playwright — all critical flows verified: login, sidebar order (Overview → Devices → Topology → Groups & Tenants → …), Add-device modal (vendor dropdown MikroTik/Huawei/Juniper/Cisco/Other; switching to Huawei hides API port + API-SSL; enabling SNMP reveals community field), non-MikroTik workspace shows only MONITORING (SNMP, Alarm Watch) + ACCESS (SSH, Telnet) — no RouterOS menus (Firewall/Hotspot count = 0), SNMP panel shows ping/CPU/sysname/interface count with 'Scan now' repopulating snmp-iface rows (2 ifaces on Lab SNMP Agent), IDC MikroTik regression: full RouterOS menus + new SNMP tab both present, Terminal (Telnet) on filtered port 1623 renders ssh-blocked-hint after failure naming outbound IP 34.16.56.64 with the correct RouterOS /ip service + /ip firewall filter commands, Topology page renders 2 nodes and 'Add link' modal opens (link-a-device, link-a-iface, etc.). Backend covered: /api/monitor/status shape + retention_days=30, /api/devices/{id}/metrics retention, GET /api/devices/{id}/snmp never leaks community (verified 'netpulse' string absent from response), PUT + scan persist, wrong community produces snmp error, GET /api/routers/{id}/resources on non-MikroTik → 400, MikroTik create without creds → 422, SNMP-enabled without community → 422, creating Huawei/Cisco/Other with SNMP at 127.0.0.1:1161/netpulse comes back status=online, topology CRUD (nodes move persists, interfaces pick-list from SNMP scan, create link + duplicate 409 + delete + render on canvas), cron /api/cron/monitor-scan bad/no token → 401 while valid token + custom X-Webhook-Id records a finished run in /api/cron/runs with result.devices/alarms/retention, TTL index on device_metrics = 30d (2592000s) and purge_history() actually deletes a 45-day-old inserted doc, public /api/public/display/{token} payload now includes topology.{nodes,links} with no credential leakage.

ui_bugs.component: SnmpPanel · CPU LOAD stat on Lab SNMP Agent
ui_bugs.issue: CPU value renders as '?%' because net-snmp on Linux does not expose hrProcessorLoad by default (WALK on 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.3.3.1.2 returns empty). Backend correctly falls back to 0, but the JSX renders `snmp.cpu ?? 0` — the '?' seen in the screenshot is actually the character '?' before '%' in the template. Consider showing '—' or '0%' when cpu is 0/missing, or hide CPU tile for hosts that don't publish the OID.

action_items: (cosmetic) SnmpPanel CPU tile displays '?%' when hrProcessorLoad OID is unavailable; render '—' when cpu is falsy so operators aren't confused.

(nice-to-have) topology.py create_link only validates that both devices are visible — it does NOT check the chosen interface actually exists in the SNMP scan, so any string is accepted for b_iface (test link used a_iface from Lab scan + arbitrary 'ether1' for IDC). Consider validating iface names against snmp_state.interfaces on link create.
critical_code_review_comments: monitor.py poll_snmp: `if not device.get('snmp_enabled') or not community: return {'error': ...}` — the caller then writes this error into db.snmp_state via update_one with $set on 'error' but does NOT wipe the previous 'interfaces' list; a device that had a successful scan and is then disabled will keep stale interfaces in the doc. Consider `$set: {error, polled_at}` and `$unset: {interfaces: '', counters: ''}` on failure.

monitor.py monitor_device: for non-MikroTik devices the status update writes 'status: online' whenever ping alive, but there is no notify_unreachable→recovery/'router-online' alarm counterpart (only unreachable). Matches iter13 behaviour but worth documenting.

monitor.py: `RETENTION_DAYS = 30` is a hard-coded constant; the plan says '30 days then deleted automatically', so this is fine, but to change retention later both the TTL index (created once) AND purge_history need to be updated together — ensure_indexes will not modify an existing index's expireAfterSeconds. Add collMod on startup or document the manual step.
topology.py create_link: no interface-existence validation as noted above; also allows creating self-loops as long as a_iface != b_iface (probably intentional but worth noting).

topology.py move_node: NodeIn accepts x/y in [-2000,4000] but there is no sanity check that the device belongs to the same workspace as the caller before upserting — visible_router does that check by throwing 404, so this is fine.
server.py grew to 638 lines (was 598) — the split noted in iter12/iter13 is still outstanding. monitor.py (283), topology.py (100), engine.py (412) are healthy.

server.py MANAGED_PUBLIC_FIELDS: 'snmp_port' is public but 'snmp_community' correctly is not. Verified GET /devices/{id}/snmp returns only {enabled, port, configured, version} — community never exposed. ✓

monitor.py cron_monitor_scan: relies on engine.cron_ack for token check + idempotency; behaviour is correct (401 on bad token, per-run recording, background scan). Timing: the platform cron X-Webhook-Id was accepted with custom value 'iter14-*' and recorded — good.

monitor.py snmp_get/snmp_walk: uses pysnmp v7 async API with lazy imports inside functions — reasonable to avoid startup cost, but `_target()` recreates the UdpTransportTarget on every call; a per-device cached target would cut per-poll latency by ~one syscall.

monitor.py poll_snmp: sums rx_mbps/tx_mbps across *all* interfaces for metric aggregation, but the user spec said 'ping every 60s, SNMP every 1 minute, interface + CPU only' — aggregating loopback (lo) into totals inflates numbers on hosts where lo shows traffic. Consider filtering out lo/loopback interfaces before summing.
sshterm.SshTerminal blocked-port hint verified live on IDC telnet 1623 — the outbound IP 34.16.56.64 and both RouterOS /ip service + /ip firewall filter commands are rendered inline. ✓

Only follow-up: (a) SnmpPanel CPU tile UX when hrProcessorLoad OID is unavailable (shows '?%'), (b) optional interface-name validation on POST /api/topology/links, (c) optional stale-interface cleanup in snmp_state on error, and (d) exclude 'lo' from rx/tx aggregation in device_metrics.
